common.search_syntax_hint: Syntax: name: / path: / new: / title: / tags: / markers: = only that column (new: = CSV “new name”, often empty until filled; title: uses scene title or file stem if title empty) · ; = and · > § | OR = or · "phrase" = exact
common.exclude_syntax_hint: Exclude uses the same syntax as search. Any row that matches the exclude box is hidden (after applying search). Leave empty to show all matches.
t1.intro: Export a file list from Stash (GraphQL findScenes). The CSV is saved as Excel-friendly UTF-8 with a BOM (byte order mark) so characters like ä, ö, ü, Ä, Ö, Ü, ß stay correct in Excel and here.
t1.hint_scan: Keep Stash updated. If you rename or move files outside Stash, run Stash → Tasks → Scan so the database matches your disk — this export only shows paths Stash already knows.
t1.hint_settings: Theme and column separator (; or ,) for saved CSV files, plus Stash URL/API for Tab 1 export: ⚙ top-right. Tabs 3 and 4 detect ; or , when you load a file. Saved CSVs use UTF-8 with BOM for Excel.
t2.intro: Scan a folder on your PC (no Stash). Produces the same CSV columns as Tab 1 so Tab 3 can open it. Unicode paths (äöü…) are kept. When you save, the separator is from ⚙ Settings; when you open a file, ; or , is detected automatically.
t2.recursive: Include files inside subfolders (all levels below the folder you pick)
t3.steps:
Steps: 1) Load CSV  2) Search  3) Preview only to test  4) Rename on disk.
Batch tools (prefix, find/replace, folder limit) sit under “Batch rules” below — open when needed. Stash connection check / CSV export test: Tab 1.
t3.section_folder_title: Rename folder on disk (dangerous) — click to open
t3.hint_csv: Load: ; or , is read from the file. Save: separator from ⚙ Settings (; or ,).
t3.filter_placeholder: e.g. name:vacation  or  name:"my clip"  or  path:4K;name:foo
t3.col.name: Current file name
t3.fr_hint: If an item already has a new file name, find/replace uses that — you can click Apply repeatedly.
t3.clear_new_names: Clear "New file name" on search matches
t3.folder_warn:
WARNING — RENAME A FOLDER (RISKY)
Renames one folder on disk. Stash, shortcuts, and this CSV will point to old paths until you run Stash → Tasks → Scan and reload the CSV. This tool cannot undo the folder rename. Use only if you understand that.
t3.fold_confirm: I understand this may break Stash paths and I will run a library scan afterward.
t3.fold_new_placeholder: new folder name only, no path
t4.intro_block:
A) Load CSV, search, set the move folder (optional subfolder), use Preview only first, then move.
B) The CSV path is your file list, not the move target. When loading, ; or , is read from the file; CSV export uses the separator in ⚙ Settings. Stash URL / API / GraphQL for exports: ⚙ Settings.
C) After moves, if Stash already knew those files: run Tasks → Scan. This tab does not call the Stash API.
t4.section_path_tips_title: Path tips (target vs list, subfolder, selected row…)
t4.where_placeholder: e.g. D:\Archive — all moved files end up here (unless checkbox below)
t4.move_hint: Default: every file you move is placed inside “Where to move files”, plus “Subfolder under that path” if you filled it (that folder is created if needed). The CSV path at the top is only the list — not the move target. Tip: “Use selected row's folder” (next to Browse) copies the parent folder of a file you selected in the list into the move target.
t4.per_source: Instead: next to each file's current folder — ignores “Where to move files” above; each file goes to <its current folder>\Subfolder\
t4.preview_only: Preview only (no moves — log what would happen)
t4.selected_only: Use selected items only (otherwise all items that match Search)
t4.preview_section_title: Move preview (first matching items — click to show or hide)
t5.intro: Proposed file names use the scene title (truncated); if the title is empty, the current file name is used — not Stash tags/markers. Tags and markers are still exported in the CSV and shown in the list for search (tags: / markers:). Optional year/rating, five custom tag slots, optional ffprobe. Pattern: ShortTitle (YYYY) - [custom] … [1080p] [rating].ext — then fill “new file name” and rename like Tab 3.
t5.hint_ffprobe: ffprobe: {exe} — after loading the CSV click «ffprobe start» (same row as the resolution options) so [1080p] etc. are filled (FFmpeg must be in PATH).
t5.hint_csv_meta: Re-export from Tab 1 / export_stash_files.ps1 for scene_date, scene_rating, scene_tags (all tag names), and scene_markers (marker titles). The year in “(YYYY)” uses scene_date when that cell has a usable year; otherwise it uses the file’s creation time on Windows, birth time on macOS when available, otherwise last modification (Linux often has no true creation time). Without title/tags/marker columns, Tab 5 falls back to the file name where needed.
t5.include_year: Year (YYYY) from CSV or file (creation if available)
t5.tag_structure_hint: Optional layout idea — e.g. slot 1=[Action], 2=[Place], 3=[Time]; slots 4–5 for extras (studio, niche, …). Only checked slots appear; order in the file name is slot 1→5, then resolution and rating.
t5.selected_only: Selected rows only — Fill and Rename apply to the highlighted rows
t5.selection_hint: Selection: Ctrl or Shift+click, or click and drag across rows (same on Tab 3 & 4).
